nodes.label: bedrock-mantle transport
nodes.rationale: AWS-recommended route and the ONLY one Gemma 4 31B supports. Configured alongside bedrock-runtime so Phase 0 can pick per arm from evidence rather than assumption, and so an adapter failure can be told apart from model weakness (spec section 6.4). Authenticates by explicit api_key on each deployment, which takes base_aws_llm.get_request_headers' api_key branch.

nodes.label: bedrock-runtime transport
nodes.rationale: Two routes wearing one prefix, chosen by model id rather than by anything in the config file. Claude models resolve to AmazonAnthropicClaudeMessagesConfig and take Invoke with a native Anthropic body, never constructing a toolUseId; everything else falls through to the openai->Converse bridge, which copies the model's own tool-call ids verbatim into toolUseId under a [a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64} class Bedrock enforces server-side. Carries no api_key so SigV4 signing is used.

nodes.label: claude-sonnet-5 deployment (mantle)
nodes.rationale: api_base deliberately omits the /v1 the endpoint actually serves: LiteLLM's anthropic provider appends '/v1/messages' itself, so the documented .../anthropic/v1 base produces a doubled /v1/v1/messages and 404s with an empty error body. Temperature/top_p/top_k are OMITTED because any non-default value returns 400 on this model, which would fail every call on the reference arm.

nodes.label: gemma-4-31b deployment (mantle)
nodes.rationale: Mantle only -- Gemma supports neither Converse nor Invoke, and its path is /openai/v1 rather than /v1. top_p is omitted under force: on 2026-08-12 the route began validating this model under OpenAI's reasoning-model contract, which rejects any non-default top_p outright, while temperature 1.0 passes and 0.6 does not. Section 5.3's constant across arms is the POLICY (lab-recommended unless the route refuses it), not the number, which is why nemotron and kimi keep top_p 0.95 rather than being levelled down. Reasoning content is returned only by the Responses API, so TokenUsage.reasoning reads zero on this path.

nodes.label: nemotron-3-super-120b deployment (mantle)
nodes.rationale: temperature 1.0 / top_p 0.95 per NVIDIA's published guidance for all tasks; path is /v1 (OpenAI Chat Completions).

nodes.label: kimi-k2-5 deployment (mantle)
nodes.rationale: temperature 1.0 / top_p 0.95 for thinking mode; Moonshot documents temperature 0 causing multi-minute stalls, which is why a single uniform sampling number across arms would be a section 5.4 failure mode.

nodes.label: claude-sonnet-5-runtime deployment
nodes.rationale: Must use the us. geo inference profile: the model card lists the In-Region runtime URL as N/A, so the bare ID cannot be invoked. US geo also matches the data-residency posture behind choosing Bedrock. No temperature/top_p -- same 400 as the mantle arm.

nodes.label: kimi-k2-5-runtime deployment (commented out)
nodes.rationale: Commented out, not deleted: it is the fallback transport if mantle ever breaks for Kimi the way it broke for Sonnet, and what it would take to restore it is worth keeping next to it. It cannot be served as written -- Kimi's tool-call ids are `functions.Read:0`, litellm sanitizes tool NAMES on the Converse path and never ids, and bakeoff.litellm_patches deliberately removed the id sanitizer (removing it is what let Kimi drive the tool loop at all), so this deployment would send a colon to Converse and fail server-side. Leaving it live left it one `--models kimi-k2-5-runtime` away from a paid run. Restoring requires an allowlist entry in CONVERSE_SAFE_TOOL_ID_MODELS with the measured id shape as evidence.

nodes.label: BAKEOFF_MANTLE_TOKEN env var name
nodes.rationale: The env var NAME is load-bearing because one proxy serves both transports. base_aws_llm.get_request_headers (verified litellm 1.95.0) uses a deployment's api_key when set, falls back to AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, and signs SigV4 only when both are absent. A proxy process with AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK set would bearer-authenticate the runtime deployments and fail every runtime arm with `bedrock:CallWithBearerToken`, while the mantle arms stay green -- reading as a bedrock-runtime problem. BAKEOFF_MANTLE_TOKEN is a name LiteLLM does not look up, so the mantle deployments name it explicitly and the runtime deployments find nothing and sign.

nodes.label: Every model_name must be distinct
nodes.rationale: LiteLLM treats repeated model_name values as one load-balanced deployment group and round-robins between them, which would randomize transport per call and confound both latency and tool-translation results. model_name also doubles as the PRICE_BOOK key in bakeoff.costs, so a name the price book does not know raises UnknownModelError mid-run. A third consequence: every model group is therefore single-deployment, which is what makes the router cooldown useless here.

nodes.label: Lab-recommended sampling policy (section 5.3)
nodes.rationale: Claude Code has no temperature flag, so the proxy config is the only layer that can set sampling. Section 5.3 says '0.6 (or lab-recommended)'; lab-recommended is what is used because a single uniform number would 400 the Sonnet arm and stall Kimi -- a config choice scored as a model difference (section 5.4). The constant held across arms is the policy, not the value, which is why config_digest deliberately excludes temperature. NOT VERIFIED in this file: LiteLLM merges litellm_params as defaults and Claude Code's own body may win, so only the wire log shows what was actually sent.

nodes.label: litellm_settings.callbacks registration (production)
nodes.rationale: Wire capture must be registered where the calls are actually made (section 6.2): the agent runs in its own container and the proxy is a third process, so a callback registered in the harness process observes nothing -- Task 11's defect 15, which produced records with empty sampling, empty prompt and tool hashes and no error status while looking complete. The dotted path must resolve to a module-level INSTANCE: get_instance_fn resolves the path with getattr and returns it as-is, then success_handler dispatches on isinstance(callback, CustomLogger), so a class object is skipped in SILENCE. bakeoff.wire.BakeoffCallback additionally cannot be named here because it needs a per-run WireLogger and run_id no config string can supply.

nodes.label: use_chat_completions_url_for_anthropic_messages
nodes.rationale: Without it LiteLLM sends any openai/ deployment's Anthropic Messages traffic to the Responses API and Bedrock answers 400 ('does not support the /v1/responses API'), measured on the Phase 0c live run 2026-08-07 for both Nemotron and Kimi. A section 6.4 adapter setting, not a model finding: the failure was identical on every candidate arm and would have read as three models unable to drive Claude Code.

nodes.label: additional_drop_params (named one at a time)
nodes.rationale: Never a blanket drop_params: true -- that would silently discard temperature or max_tokens if a provider rejected one, leaving section 5.3 sampling unapplied with nothing in the record saying so. context_management and output_config are turned into an anthropic-beta header by LiteLLM and mantle answers 'invalid beta flag'. CORRECTION 2026-08-12: reasoning_effort was NOT a Bedrock rejection -- probed with raw httpx, Bedrock ACCEPTS it on all three candidates and 'high' measurably changes output (gemma 240->580, kimi 171->717 completion tokens). The rejection is litellm's own _check_valid_arg because OpenAIGPTConfig.get_supported_openai_params omits it for a non-o-series model. The entry is kept as a backstop so a patch that fails to apply produces a loud UnsupportedParamsError rather than silently forwarding the 'medium' litellm derives from Claude Code's thinking: {type: adaptive}.

nodes.label: router_settings.disable_cooldowns (production)
nodes.rationale: Measured against litellm 1.95.0: _should_cooldown_deployment has four branches, three guarded by is_single_deployment_model_group and the fourth (elif litellm._should_retry(status_code) is False) is not. _should_retry(401) and (403) are both False, so ONE auth failure cools the deployment down for 5 s. Every model group is single-deployment by design, so there is nothing to fail over to; num_retries: 3 then retries into the cooldown and gets RouterRateLimitError, a plain ValueError with NO status_code, so the wire log's last entry reads 'No deployments available' at status None instead of naming the credential problem. The other unguarded branch needs 1000 requests in a minute and is unreachable. Applied to every deployment identically, so not a section 5.3 divergence.

nodes.label: general_settings.num_retries: 3
nodes.rationale: Retries are logged as infra events, never silently absorbed. Each retry is its own callback invocation, which is why the wire log counts calls rather than turns.

nodes.label: bakeoff.proxy_callback.instance
nodes.rationale: Exists as a module-level object precisely so a config line can point at an instance rather than a type -- LiteLLM's get_instance_fn resolves the dotted path with getattr and dispatches on isinstance(callback, CustomLogger), skipping a class in silence. Attributes each call by the X-Bakeoff-Run-Id header the harness stamps per run; the harness replays those lines through WireLogger afterwards so there is exactly one canonical artifact.

nodes.label: bakeoff.litellm_patches.instance
nodes.rationale: Applies its patches on construction and is imported by nothing in the harness -- that separation is what keeps the harness process's litellm unpatched. Not optional in ANY config: the tool-id patch must be present wherever a proxy is started, or the offline gate and the fault-injection suite certify an UNPATCHED topology under the same name as the patched one. Carries the max_tokens->max_completion_tokens rename and the reasoning_effort='none' pin, neither of which can be expressed in config because a drop cannot express a value.

nodes.label: bakeoff.costs PRICE_BOOK
nodes.rationale: Keyed on the proxy config's model_name, so every deployment name in every config file is simultaneously a pricing key. A name the price book does not know raises UnknownModelError mid-run; assemble_record catches it and the record survives with turns, tokens and cost all zero.
